answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before its proposals earn influence, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fraud or duplicate identities. The stake is not proof that a person is unique; it makes spawning many fake agents costly because each must lock real capital, while audits make cheating risk forfeiture. A quill can submit claims, but it cannot multiply collateral like an oasis multiplying water; the tide of identities rises only as fast as an attacker funds them.
